source.text: וַֽיהוָ֛ה פָּקַ֥ד אֶת־שָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמָ֑ר וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה לְשָׂרָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And YHWH visited Sarah as he had said, and did YHWH to Sarah as he had spoken.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} visited Sarah as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did to Sarah as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} took note of Sarah as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} carried out for Sarah what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} came to help Sarah, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said. He kept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise to her.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} visitó a Sara como había dicho, e hizo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} con Sara como había hablado.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se ocupó de Sara tal como había dicho que lo haría, y cumplió con Sara lo que había prometido.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vino a ayudar a Sara, como había dicho. Cumplió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} promesa.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} visita Sara comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait dit, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fit pour Sara comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait déclaré.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} intervint en faveur de Sara, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait annoncé, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} accomplit pour elle ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est venu en aide à Sara, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’avait dit. Il a tenu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} promesse envers elle.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjilia Sara kama alivyosema, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtendea Sara kama alivyonena.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimkumbuka Sara kama alivyokuwa amesema, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtimizia Sara yale aliyokuwa ameahidi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimsaidia Sara, kama alivyokuwa amesema. Akatimiza ahadi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwake.

decisions.choice: visited (paqad): came to act on her behalf
decisions.reason: When God 'visits' someone he turns his attention to them and acts, in blessing or in judgment. The same verb is used when God gives Hannah children (1 Samuel 2:21) and when Joseph says God will come to Israel's aid (50:24).

decisions.choice: as he had said: the promise of 17:19-21 and 18:10-14
decisions.reason: The words are repeated twice over: what God said, he did. The son promised for 'this time next year' (17:21; 18:14) is born.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("visita", "intervint"), passé composé at Readable ("est venu en aide")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets out: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and read in school today, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַתַּהַר֩ וַתֵּ֨לֶד שָׂרָ֧ה לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם בֵּ֖ן לִזְקֻנָ֑יו לַמּוֹעֵ֕ד אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And conceived and bore Sarah to Abraham a son for his old age, at the appointed time which had spoken to him God.

en.L: And Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.
en.B: Sarah conceived, and when Abraham was old she gave him a son, at the set time God had told him of.
en.R: Sarah became pregnant and had a baby boy, even though Abraham was very old. It happened at the exact time God had said it would.

es.L: Y concibió y dio a luz Sara a Abraham un hijo en su vejez, en el tiempo señalado del que Dios le había hablado.
es.B: Sara quedó embarazada y, siendo Abraham ya anciano, le dio un hijo en el momento que Dios le había anunciado.
es.R: Sara quedó embarazada y tuvo un niño, aunque Abraham era muy viejo. Ocurrió justo en el tiempo que Dios había dicho.

fr.L: Et Sara conçut et enfanta à Abraham un fils dans sa vieillesse, au moment fixé dont Dieu lui avait parlé.
fr.B: Sara devint enceinte et, alors qu’Abraham était âgé, elle lui donna un fils, au moment que Dieu lui avait fixé.
fr.R: Sara a été enceinte et elle a eu un petit garçon, alors qu’Abraham était très vieux. C’est arrivé exactement au moment que Dieu avait annoncé.

sw.L: Naye Sara akapata mimba, akamzalia Abrahamu mwana katika uzee wake, wakati ule uliowekwa ambao Mungu alimwambia.
sw.B: Sara alipata mimba, na Abrahamu akiwa mzee, akamzalia mwana, wakati ule ule ambao Mungu alikuwa amemtajia.
sw.R: Sara alipata mimba, akazaa mtoto wa kiume, ingawa Abrahamu alikuwa mzee sana. Ilitokea wakati ule hasa ambao Mungu alikuwa amesema.

decisions.choice: the appointed time: the time God had set
decisions.reason: The word (mo'ed) is the one used in 17:21 and 18:14: 'at the appointed time I will return to you'. God kept his own schedule.

decisions.choice: his old age
decisions.reason: Abraham is 100 (verse 5) and Sarah ninety (17:17). The birth is beyond what nature allows, as Sarah herself had said (18:11-12).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶֽת־שֶׁם־בְּנ֧וֹ הַנּֽוֹלַד־ל֛וֹ אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָה־לּ֥וֹ שָׂרָ֖ה יִצְחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Abraham the name of his son who was born to him, whom bore to him Sarah, Isaac.

en.L: And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
en.B: Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son who had been born to him, the son Sarah bore him.
en.R: Abraham named the baby Isaac, as God had told him to.

es.L: Y llamó Abraham el nombre de su hijo que le había nacido, que Sara le dio a luz, Isaac.
es.B: Abraham le puso por nombre Isaac al hijo que le había nacido, el hijo que Sara le dio.
es.R: Abraham le puso al niño el nombre de Isaac, como Dios le había dicho.

fr.L: Et Abraham appela du nom d’Isaac son fils qui lui était né, que Sara lui avait enfanté.
fr.B: Abraham donna le nom d’Isaac au fils qui lui était né, celui que Sara lui avait donné.
fr.R: Abraham a appelé le bébé Isaac, comme Dieu le lui avait dit.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akamwita jina mwanawe aliyezaliwa kwake, ambaye Sara alimzalia, Isaka.
sw.B: Abrahamu akampa jina Isaka yule mwana aliyezaliwa kwake, mwana ambaye Sara alimzalia.
sw.R: Abrahamu akamwita mtoto huyo Isaka, kama Mungu alivyokuwa amemwambia.

decisions.choice: Isaac: 'he laughs'
decisions.reason: The name (Yitschaq) means 'he laughs'. Abraham laughed at the promise (17:17), and Sarah did too (18:12-15); God chose the name (17:19). In verses 6 and 9 the word for laughter comes back.

decisions.choice: as God had told him to
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that God gave the name (17:19).

source.text: וַיָּ֤מָל אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַ֖ת יָמִ֑ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And circumcised Abraham Isaac his son [as] a son of eight days, as had commanded him God.

en.L: And Abraham circumcised Isaac his son when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
en.B: Abraham circumcised his son Isaac on the eighth day after his birth, following God's command.
en.R: When Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him. God had told him to do this.

es.L: Y circuncidó Abraham a Isaac su hijo a los ocho días, como Dios le había mandado.
es.B: Abraham circuncidó a su hijo Isaac al octavo día de nacer, conforme al mandato de Dios.
es.R: Cuando Isaac tenía ocho días, Abraham lo circuncidó. Dios le había dicho que lo hiciera.

fr.L: Et Abraham circoncit Isaac son fils, [âgé] de huit jours, comme Dieu le lui avait commandé.
fr.B: Abraham circoncit son fils Isaac le huitième jour après sa naissance, selon l’ordre de Dieu.
fr.R: Quand Isaac a eu huit jours, Abraham l’a circoncis. Dieu lui avait dit de le faire.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akamtahiri Isaka mwanawe [alipokuwa] mwana wa siku nane, kama Mungu alivyomwamuru.
sw.B: Abrahamu alimtahiri mwanawe Isaka siku ya nane baada ya kuzaliwa kwake, kwa kufuata agizo la Mungu.
sw.R: Isaka alipokuwa na umri wa siku nane, Abrahamu alimtahiri. Mungu alikuwa amemwambia afanye hivyo.

decisions.choice: eight days old: the sign of the covenant
decisions.reason: God had commanded that every boy be circumcised on the eighth day as the sign of his covenant (17:10-12). Isaac is the first child to receive it at the age the command set.

source.text: וְאַבְרָהָ֖ם בֶּן־מְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה בְּהִוָּ֣לֶד ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֥ק בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abraham [was] a son of a hundred years when was born to him Isaac his son.

en.L: And Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac his son was born to him.
en.B: Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born.
en.R: Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born.

es.L: Y Abraham [tenía] cien años cuando le nació Isaac su hijo.
es.B: Abraham tenía cien años cuando nació su hijo Isaac.
es.R: Abraham tenía cien años cuando nació su hijo Isaac.

fr.L: Et Abraham [était] âgé de cent ans quand lui naquit Isaac son fils.
fr.B: Abraham avait cent ans quand son fils Isaac lui naquit.
fr.R: Abraham avait cent ans quand son fils Isaac est né.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu [alikuwa] mwana wa miaka mia moja alipozaliwa Isaka mwanawe.
sw.B: Abrahamu alikuwa na umri wa miaka mia moja mwanawe Isaka alipozaliwa.
sw.R: Abrahamu alikuwa na miaka mia moja mwanawe Isaka alipozaliwa.

decisions.choice: 100 years old: twenty-five years of waiting
decisions.reason: Abraham was seventy-five when God first promised to make him a great nation (12:2-4). The son of the promise comes twenty-five years later.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר שָׂרָ֔ה צְחֹ֕ק עָ֥שָׂה לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים כָּל־הַשֹּׁמֵ֖עַ יִֽצְחַק־לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Sarah, laughter has made for me God; everyone who hears will laugh for me.

en.L: And Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me."
en.B: Sarah said, "God has given me reason to laugh, and all who hear of it will share my laughter."
en.R: Sarah said, "God has made me laugh with joy! Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."

es.L: Y dijo Sara: «Risa me ha hecho Dios; todo el que [lo] oiga se reirá conmigo».
es.B: Sara dijo: «Dios me ha dado motivo para reír, y todos los que se enteren reirán conmigo».
es.R: Sara dijo: «¡Dios me ha hecho reír de alegría! Todos los que sepan esto se van a reír conmigo».

fr.L: Et Sara dit : « Dieu m’a fait un rire ; quiconque [l’]entendra rira avec moi. »
fr.B: Sara dit : « Dieu m’a donné de quoi rire, et tous ceux qui l’apprendront partageront mon rire. »
fr.R: Sara a dit : « Dieu m’a fait rire de joie ! Tous ceux qui l’apprendront riront avec moi. »

sw.L: Naye Sara akasema, "Mungu amenifanyia kicheko; kila asikiaye atacheka pamoja nami."
sw.B: Sara akasema, "Mungu amenipa sababu ya kucheka, na wote watakaosikia habari hii watacheka pamoja nami."
sw.R: Sara akasema, "Mungu amenifanya nicheke kwa furaha! Kila mtu atakayesikia jambo hili atacheka pamoja nami."

decisions.choice: laughter (tsechoq): the name Isaac
decisions.reason: The word is the root of Isaac's name. Sarah's laughter of disbelief (18:12) has become the laughter of joy.

decisions.choice: laugh with me: or laugh at me
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that people will rejoice with Sarah, or that they will laugh at an old woman with a baby. The joy of the verse makes the first more likely; Sarah may also mean both.

source.text: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֤י מִלֵּל֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם הֵינִ֥יקָה בָנִ֖ים שָׂרָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי בֵ֖ן לִזְקֻנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, who would have said to Abraham, Sarah has nursed children? For I have borne a son for his old age.

en.L: And she said, "Who would have said to Abraham, 'Sarah will nurse children'? Yet I have borne [him] a son in his old age."
en.B: She went on, "Who would have dared to tell Abraham, 'Sarah will be nursing babies'? But now, when he is old, I have borne him a son!"
en.R: She also said, "No one would have dreamed of telling Abraham that Sarah would ever nurse a baby. But I have had a son for him, even though he is old!"

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Quién le habría dicho a Abraham: “Sara amamantará hijos”? Pues yo [le] he dado a luz un hijo en su vejez».
es.B: Y añadió: «¿Quién se habría atrevido a decirle a Abraham: “Sara va a amamantar niños”? ¡Pero ahora, ya anciano él, le he dado un hijo!».
es.R: También dijo: «A nadie se le habría ocurrido decirle a Abraham que Sara llegaría a dar el pecho a un bebé. ¡Pero le he dado un hijo, aunque él es viejo!».

fr.L: Et elle dit : « Qui aurait dit à Abraham : “Sara allaitera des enfants” ? Or je [lui] ai enfanté un fils dans sa vieillesse. »
fr.B: Elle ajouta : « Qui aurait osé dire à Abraham : “Sara allaitera des enfants” ? Et pourtant, dans sa vieillesse, je lui ai donné un fils ! »
fr.R: Elle a dit aussi : « Personne n’aurait imaginé dire à Abraham que Sara donnerait un jour le sein à un bébé. Mais je lui ai donné un fils, alors qu’il est vieux ! »

sw.L: Akasema, "Nani angemwambia Abrahamu, 'Sara atanyonyesha watoto'? Lakini nimemzalia mwana katika uzee wake."
sw.B: Akaendelea kusema, "Nani angethubutu kumwambia Abrahamu, 'Sara atanyonyesha watoto'? Lakini sasa, akiwa mzee, nimemzalia mwana!"
sw.R: Pia akasema, "Hakuna mtu ambaye angefikiri kumwambia Abrahamu kwamba Sara angenyonyesha mtoto. Lakini nimemzalia mwana, ingawa yeye ni mzee!"

decisions.choice: would have said (millel): a poetic word
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and belongs to poetry. Sarah's words are a little song of wonder, like Hannah's (1 Samuel 2:1-10).

decisions.choice: nurse children: plural for one son
decisions.reason: The plural states the general idea: Sarah a nursing mother at all. Only one son is meant.

source.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֥ל הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַיִּגָּמַ֑ל וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אַבְרָהָם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֔וֹל בְּי֖וֹם הִגָּמֵ֥ל אֶת־יִצְחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And grew the child and was weaned, and made Abraham a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

en.L: And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.
en.B: The boy grew older, and Abraham celebrated the day of his weaning with a large feast.
en.R: Isaac grew. When he was old enough to stop nursing, Abraham gave a big party to celebrate.

es.L: Y creció el niño y fue destetado, y Abraham hizo un gran banquete el día en que Isaac fue destetado.
es.B: El niño fue creciendo, y el día en que lo destetaron Abraham lo celebró con un gran banquete.
es.R: Isaac creció. Cuando ya tuvo edad para dejar de mamar, Abraham hizo una gran fiesta para celebrarlo.

fr.L: Et l’enfant grandit et fut sevré, et Abraham fit un grand festin le jour où Isaac fut sevré.
fr.B: L’enfant grandit, et Abraham célébra par un grand festin le jour de son sevrage.
fr.R: Isaac a grandi. Quand il a été assez grand pour ne plus téter, Abraham a fait une grande fête pour le célébrer.

sw.L: Naye mtoto akakua, akaachishwa kunyonya, na Abrahamu akafanya karamu kubwa siku ile Isaka alipoachishwa kunyonya.
sw.B: Mtoto alikua, na siku alipoachishwa kunyonya Abrahamu akaisherehekea kwa karamu kubwa.
sw.R: Isaka alikua. Alipofikia umri wa kuacha kunyonya, Abrahamu alifanya sherehe kubwa.

decisions.choice: weaned: two or three years old
decisions.reason: Children were nursed much longer than today, often for two or three years (1 Samuel 1:22-24; 2 Maccabees 7:27). Surviving early childhood was a reason to celebrate.

source.text: וַתֵּ֨רֶא שָׂרָ֜ה אֶֽת־בֶּן־הָגָ֧ר הַמִּצְרִ֛ית אֲשֶׁר־יָלְדָ֥ה לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם מְצַחֵֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Sarah the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.

en.L: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, laughing.
en.B: Then Sarah saw the son that Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham poking fun.
en.R: Sarah saw Ishmael mocking Isaac. Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar, the woman from Egypt.

es.L: Y vio Sara al hijo de Agar la egipcia, el que ella le había dado a luz a Abraham, riéndose.
es.B: Entonces Sara vio que el hijo que Agar la egipcia le había dado a Abraham se estaba burlando.
es.R: Sara vio que Ismael se burlaba de Isaac. Ismael era hijo de Abraham y de Agar, la mujer egipcia.

fr.L: Et Sara vit le fils d’Agar l’Égyptienne, qu’elle avait enfanté à Abraham, en train de rire.
fr.B: Puis Sara vit le fils qu’Agar l’Égyptienne avait donné à Abraham en train de se moquer.
fr.R: Sara a vu Ismaël se moquer d’Isaac. Ismaël était le fils d’Abraham et d’Agar, la femme venue d’Égypte.

sw.L: Naye Sara akamwona mwana wa Hajiri Mmisri, ambaye alikuwa amemzalia Abrahamu, akicheka.
sw.B: Kisha Sara akamwona yule mwana ambaye Hajiri Mmisri alimzalia Abrahamu akifanya dhihaka.
sw.R: Sara alimwona Ishmaeli akimdhihaki Isaka. Ishmaeli alikuwa mwana wa Abrahamu kwa Hajiri, yule mwanamke kutoka Misri.

decisions.choice: laughing (metsaheq): mocking, or playing
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of 'laugh', the root of Isaac's name once more. It can mean to laugh, to play, or to make fun of (19:14; 39:14). Sarah's reaction suggests mockery, and Galatians 4:29 speaks of the son of the slave woman persecuting the son of the promise. Others read it as harmless play that showed Sarah the son of the slave on equal terms with Isaac.

decisions.choice: laughing: the Septuagint adds 'with Isaac her son'
decisions.reason: The Greek Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate read 'playing with Isaac her son'. The Hebrew text, followed here, has no object.

decisions.choice: the son of Hagar: Ishmael is not named
decisions.reason: In this chapter Ishmael is never named; he is 'the son of Hagar', 'the son of the slave woman', 'the boy'. The silence keeps the story's focus on how Sarah and Abraham see him. His name, 'God hears', is echoed when God hears him (verse 17).

decisions.choice: Ishmael ... of Isaac
decisions.reason: Readable names the boy and supplies the object of the mocking. The object is implied by Sarah's reply (verse 10) but not stated in the Hebrew (m1, m2).

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְאַבְרָהָ֔ם גָּרֵ֛שׁ הָאָמָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את וְאֶת־בְּנָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִירַשׁ֙ בֶּן־הָאָמָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את עִם־בְּנִ֖י עִם־יִצְחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to Abraham, drive out this slave woman and her son, for will not inherit [the] son of this slave woman with my son, with Isaac.

en.L: And she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son, with Isaac."
en.B: and she told Abraham, "Send this slave woman and her boy away! No son of this slave is going to be an heir alongside my son Isaac."
en.R: She said to Abraham, "Make this slave woman and her son leave! Her son must not get any share of what is yours when you die. It is all for my son Isaac."

es.L: Y dijo a Abraham: «Echa fuera a esta esclava y a su hijo, porque el hijo de esta esclava no heredará con mi hijo, con Isaac».
es.B: y le dijo a Abraham: «¡Despide a esta esclava y a su muchacho! El hijo de esta esclava no va a heredar junto con mi hijo Isaac».
es.R: Le dijo a Abraham: «¡Haz que se vayan esta esclava y su hijo! Su hijo no debe recibir nada de lo tuyo cuando mueras. Todo es para mi hijo Isaac».

fr.L: Et elle dit à Abraham : « Chasse cette esclave et son fils, car le fils de cette esclave n’héritera pas avec mon fils, avec Isaac. »
fr.B: et elle dit à Abraham : « Renvoie cette esclave et son garçon ! Le fils de cette esclave ne sera pas héritier à côté de mon fils Isaac. »
fr.R: Elle a dit à Abraham : « Fais partir cette esclave et son fils ! Son fils ne doit rien recevoir de tes biens quand tu mourras. Tout est pour mon fils Isaac. »

sw.L: Akamwambia Abrahamu, "Mfukuze mjakazi huyu pamoja na mwanawe, kwa maana mwana wa mjakazi huyu hatarithi pamoja na mwanangu, pamoja na Isaka."
sw.B: akamwambia Abrahamu, "Mfukuze mjakazi huyu na mvulana wake! Mwana wa mjakazi huyu hatakuwa mrithi pamoja na mwanangu Isaka."
sw.R: Akamwambia Abrahamu, "Mwondoe mjakazi huyu na mwanawe! Mwanawe asipate sehemu yoyote ya mali yako utakapokufa. Yote ni ya mwanangu Isaka."

decisions.choice: drive out (garesh): expel for good
decisions.reason: The verb is used for God driving the man from the garden (3:24) and for divorce (Leviticus 21:7). Sarah demands a permanent break.

decisions.choice: this slave woman (amah): Sarah does not use her name
decisions.reason: Sarah speaks of 'this slave woman' and 'her son', never Hagar or Ishmael. The word amah means a female slave, like shifchah in 16:1.

decisions.choice: shall not be heir with my son: the firstborn's share
decisions.reason: Ishmael was Abraham's firstborn. A son born to a slave woman could be counted as an heir, which is why Sarah wants him sent away. Later law protected a firstborn son from being passed over (Deuteronomy 21:15-17).

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: Sarah's demand turns on Hagar's son being a slave's son, not an heir beside the free woman's son (m3; Galatians 4:30).

decisions.choice: "mjakazi" (slave woman) at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili has its own word for a female slave, "mjakazi", which keeps the contrast between slave and free that the English keeps with "slave woman" at every level. Where the English Balanced and Readable say "servant" (verse 12), Swahili says "mtumishi wa kike".

source.text: וַיֵּ֧רַע הַדָּבָ֛ר מְאֹ֖ד בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם עַ֖ל אוֹדֹ֥ת בְּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was evil the matter exceedingly in [the] eyes of Abraham on account of his son.

en.L: And the matter was very evil in the eyes of Abraham on account of his son.
en.B: This grieved Abraham deeply, since it was his own son at stake.
en.R: This troubled Abraham greatly. After all, Ishmael was his son too.

es.L: Y el asunto fue muy malo a los ojos de Abraham a causa de su hijo.
es.B: Esto le dolió profundamente a Abraham, pues se trataba de su propio hijo.
es.R: Esto le preocupó mucho a Abraham. Al fin y al cabo, Ismael también era su hijo.

fr.L: Et la chose fut très mauvaise aux yeux d’Abraham à cause de son fils.
fr.B: Cela affligea profondément Abraham, car il s’agissait de son propre fils.
fr.R: Cela a beaucoup tourmenté Abraham. Après tout, Ismaël était aussi son fils.

sw.L: Na jambo hilo likawa baya sana machoni pa Abrahamu kwa ajili ya mwanawe.
sw.B: Jambo hilo lilimhuzunisha Abrahamu sana, kwa kuwa lilimhusu mwanawe mwenyewe.
sw.R: Jambo hilo lilimsumbua Abrahamu sana. Hata hivyo, Ishmaeli pia alikuwa mwanawe.

decisions.choice: very evil in his eyes: deeply distressing to him
decisions.reason: 'Evil in the eyes of' means displeasing, distressing. Abraham loved Ishmael (17:18).

decisions.choice: Ishmael
decisions.reason: Readable names the son so the reader knows which son is meant.

records.literal_gloss: And said God to Abraham, let it not be evil in your eyes on account of the lad and on account of your slave woman; all that says to you Sarah, listen to her voice, for in Isaac will be called to you offspring.

en.L: But God said to Abraham, "Do not let it be evil in your eyes on account of the boy and on account of your slave woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for through Isaac offspring shall be named for you.
en.B: But God told Abraham, "Do not be troubled about the boy and your servant. Do as Sarah says, in everything. The descendants who will carry your name will come through Isaac.
en.R: God said to Abraham, "Do not be upset about the boy and your servant. Do what Sarah tells you. The descendants I promised you will come through Isaac.

es.L: Pero dijo Dios a Abraham: «No sea malo a tus ojos a causa del muchacho y a causa de tu esclava. En todo lo que te diga Sara, escucha su voz, porque por medio de Isaac te será nombrada descendencia.
es.B: Pero Dios le dijo a Abraham: «No te angusties por el muchacho ni por tu sierva. Haz en todo lo que Sara te diga. Los descendientes que llevarán tu nombre vendrán por medio de Isaac.
es.R: Dios le dijo a Abraham: «No te preocupes por el muchacho ni por tu sierva. Haz lo que Sara te dice. Los descendientes que te prometí vendrán por medio de Isaac.

fr.L: Mais Dieu dit à Abraham : « Que cela ne soit pas mauvais à tes yeux à cause du garçon et à cause de ton esclave. Tout ce que Sara te dira, écoute sa voix, car c’est par Isaac qu’une descendance sera nommée pour toi.
fr.B: Mais Dieu dit à Abraham : « Ne te tourmente pas pour le garçon et pour ta servante. Fais en tout ce que Sara te dit. C’est par Isaac que viendra la descendance qui portera ton nom.
fr.R: Dieu a dit à Abraham : « Ne t’inquiète pas pour le garçon et pour ta servante. Fais ce que Sara te dit. Les descendants que je t’ai promis viendront par Isaac.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu akamwambia Abrahamu, "Lisiwe baya machoni pako kwa ajili ya kijana na kwa ajili ya mjakazi wako. Kila neno Sara atakalokuambia, isikilize sauti yake, kwa maana katika Isaka uzao utaitwa kwa ajili yako.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu akamwambia Abrahamu, "Usisumbuke kwa ajili ya kijana na mtumishi wako wa kike. Fanya kila jambo Sara analokuambia. Wazao watakaoitwa kwa jina lako watatoka kwa Isaka.
sw.R: Mungu akamwambia Abrahamu, "Usihuzunike kwa ajili ya kijana na mtumishi wako wa kike. Fanya kile Sara anachokuambia. Wazao niliokuahidi watatoka kwa Isaka.

decisions.choice: through Isaac offspring shall be named for you: Isaac carries the promise
decisions.reason: The offspring who will be called Abraham's, in the sense of the promise, will be counted through Isaac. Paul quotes the words in Romans 9:7, and Hebrews 11:18 recalls them in speaking of Abraham's test in chapter 22.

decisions.choice: listen to her voice: God sides with Sarah's demand, for his own reasons
decisions.reason: God tells Abraham to do what Sarah says, but gives his own reason and his own promise for Ishmael (verse 13). Earlier, listening to Sarah's voice had led to trouble (16:2).

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in this translation, zera is 'offspring' in Literal and 'descendants' in Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וְגַ֥ם אֶת־בֶּן־הָאָמָ֖ה לְג֣וֹי אֲשִׂימֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֥י זַרְעֲךָ֖ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And also the son of the slave woman into a nation I will make him, for your offspring [is] he.

en.L: And also the son of the slave woman I will make into a nation, for he is your offspring."
en.B: But I will make the slave woman's son into a nation as well, because he too is your child."
en.R: I will make a nation from the slave woman's son too, because he is also your son."

es.L: Y también al hijo de la esclava lo haré una nación, porque él es tu descendencia».
es.B: Pero también del hijo de la esclava haré una nación, porque él también es hijo tuyo».
es.R: Del hijo de la esclava también haré una nación, porque él también es tu hijo».

fr.L: Et du fils de l’esclave aussi je ferai une nation, car il est ta descendance. »
fr.B: Mais du fils de l’esclave aussi je ferai une nation, car lui aussi est ton enfant. »
fr.R: Je ferai aussi une nation avec le fils de l’esclave, parce que lui aussi est ton fils. »

sw.L: Na pia mwana wa mjakazi nitamfanya kuwa taifa, kwa sababu yeye ni uzao wako."
sw.B: Lakini mwana wa mjakazi pia nitamfanya kuwa taifa, kwa sababu yeye naye ni mtoto wako."
sw.R: Nitamfanya mwana wa mjakazi pia kuwa taifa, kwa sababu naye ni mwanao."

decisions.choice: I will make him a nation: a promise for Ishmael
decisions.reason: God repeats his promise to Hagar (16:10) and to Abraham (17:20). Ishmael is sent away, but not abandoned; for Abraham's sake he too has a future.

decisions.choice: your child (B), your son (R)
decisions.reason: Zera here means one person, Ishmael, so Balanced and Readable say 'child' or 'son' rather than the plural 'descendants'.

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as in verse 10: the phrase marks Ishmael as a slave's son, set against Isaac the free woman's son and heir (Galatians 4:22-23), so the style guide keeps the word.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֣ם אַבְרָהָ֣ם׀בַּבֹּ֡קֶר וַיִּֽקַּֽח־לֶחֶם֩ וְחֵ֨מַת מַ֜יִם וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־הָ֠גָר שָׂ֧ם עַל־שִׁכְמָ֛הּ וְאֶת־הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֶ֑הָ וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ וַתֵּ֔תַע בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early Abraham in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave [them] to Hagar, putting [them] on her shoulder, and the boy, and sent her away; and she went and wandered in [the] wilderness of Beersheba.

en.L: So Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water and gave [them] to Hagar, putting [them] on her shoulder, and the boy, and he sent her away. And she went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
en.B: Abraham was up at dawn. He took food and a skin of water and handed them to Hagar, setting them on her shoulder; he handed over the boy too, and sent her away. She left and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
en.R: Abraham got up early the next morning. He gave Hagar some food and a leather bag full of water. He put them on her shoulder and sent her away with her son. She went off and wandered in the desert near Beersheba.

es.L: Y madrugó Abraham por la mañana, y tomó pan y un odre de agua y [se los] dio a Agar, poniéndo[los] sobre su hombro, y al muchacho, y la despidió. Y ella se fue y anduvo errante por el desierto de Beerseba.
es.B: Abraham se levantó al amanecer. Tomó comida y un odre de agua y se los entregó a Agar, colocándoselos sobre el hombro; le entregó también al muchacho y la despidió. Ella se marchó y anduvo sin rumbo por el desierto de Beerseba.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, Abraham se levantó temprano. Le dio a Agar algo de comida y una bolsa de cuero llena de agua. Se lo puso todo al hombro y la despidió con su hijo. Ella se fue y anduvo perdida por el desierto, cerca de Beerseba.

fr.L: Et Abraham se leva tôt le matin, et il prit du pain et une outre d’eau et [les] donna à Agar, [les] mettant sur son épaule, ainsi que l’enfant, et il la renvoya. Et elle s’en alla et erra dans le désert de Beer-Shéba.
fr.B: Abraham se leva à l’aube. Il prit de la nourriture et une outre d’eau et les remit à Agar en les lui posant sur l’épaule ; il lui confia aussi le garçon, puis il la renvoya. Elle partit et erra dans le désert de Beer-Shéba.
fr.R: Le lendemain, Abraham s’est levé tôt. Il a donné à Agar un peu de nourriture et une outre en cuir pleine d’eau. Il les lui a mises sur l’épaule et l’a renvoyée avec son fils. Elle est partie et elle a erré dans le désert, près de Beer-Shéba.

sw.L: Basi Abrahamu akaamka mapema asubuhi, akachukua mkate na kiriba cha maji, akampa Hajiri, akaviweka begani mwake, pamoja na mtoto, akamwacha aende zake. Naye akaenda, akatangatanga katika nyika ya Beer-sheba.
sw.B: Abrahamu aliamka alfajiri. Akachukua chakula na kiriba cha maji, akampa Hajiri, akamtwika begani; akamkabidhi pia kijana, akamwacha aende. Hajiri akaondoka, akatangatanga katika nyika ya Beer-sheba.
sw.R: Kesho yake asubuhi na mapema Abrahamu aliamka. Akampa Hajiri chakula kidogo na mfuko wa ngozi uliojaa maji. Akamtwika begani, akamwacha aondoke pamoja na mwanawe. Hajiri akaenda zake, akatangatanga jangwani karibu na Beer-sheba.

decisions.choice: a skin of water: a leather water bag
decisions.reason: Water was carried in a bag made from a goatskin. One skin would not last long in the desert.

decisions.choice: putting them on her shoulder, and the boy: who carries what
alternatives: putting them and the boy on her shoulder
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read as Abraham putting the food and water on her shoulder and giving her the boy, or as putting the boy too on her shoulder. Ishmael was about sixteen (16:16; 21:5, 8), which makes the first reading more likely; the second would picture him as a child.

decisions.choice: sent her away ... wandered
decisions.reason: 'Sent away' (shillach) is the word used for releasing a slave or divorcing a wife (Deuteronomy 15:13; 24:1). 'Wandered' is the word Abraham used of his own travels (20:13), and can also mean to lose one's way.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Beersheba: the dry land around Beersheba
decisions.reason: The place gets its name later in this chapter (verse 31); the narrator uses the name the reader knows.

source.text: וַיִּכְל֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מִן־הַחֵ֑מֶת וַתַּשְׁלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־הַיֶּ֔לֶד תַּ֖חַת אַחַ֥ד הַשִּׂיחִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And were finished the water from the skin, and she threw the boy under one of the bushes.

en.L: And the water in the skin was used up, and she cast the boy under one of the bushes.
en.B: Once the skin had no water left, she laid the boy down under one of the shrubs.
en.R: Before long the water ran out. Hagar left her son lying under a bush, out of the sun.

es.L: Y se acabó el agua del odre, y ella arrojó al muchacho debajo de uno de los arbustos.
es.B: Cuando el odre se quedó sin agua, ella dejó al muchacho debajo de uno de los matorrales.
es.R: Al poco tiempo se acabó el agua. Agar dejó a su hijo tendido bajo un arbusto, a la sombra.

fr.L: Et l’eau de l’outre s’épuisa, et elle jeta l’enfant sous l’un des arbrisseaux.
fr.B: Quand l’outre fut vide, elle déposa le garçon sous l’un des buissons.
fr.R: Bientôt, il n’y a plus eu d’eau. Agar a couché son fils sous un buisson, à l’abri du soleil.

sw.L: Na maji yakaisha katika kiriba, naye akamtupa mtoto chini ya kichaka kimojawapo.
sw.B: Maji ya kiriba yalipokwisha, alimlaza kijana chini ya kichaka kimoja.
sw.R: Baada ya muda mfupi maji yakaisha. Hajiri akamlaza mwanawe chini ya kichaka, kivulini.

decisions.choice: cast (hishlikh): put down quickly
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to throw (37:22). Here it describes Hagar setting the exhausted boy down in haste and despair, perhaps after supporting him.

decisions.choice: laid down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'laid down', since 'threw' would suggest violence (m1).

decisions.choice: out of the sun
decisions.reason: The point of putting him under a bush is shade from the sun; Readable says so.

source.text: וַתֵּלֶךְ֩ וַתֵּ֨שֶׁב לָ֜הּ מִנֶּ֗גֶד הַרְחֵק֙ כִּמְטַחֲוֵ֣י קֶ֔שֶׁת כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֔ה אַל־אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּמ֣וֹת הַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־קֹלָ֖הּ וַתֵּֽבְךְּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went and sat down by herself opposite, at a distance like shooters of a bow, for she said, let me not look on the death of the boy. And she sat opposite, and lifted up her voice and wept.

en.L: And she went and sat down by herself opposite [him], a good way off, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not look on the death of the child." And she sat opposite [him], and lifted up her voice and wept.
en.B: She moved away and sat down across from him at about the distance an arrow flies. "I will not watch while the boy dies," she said to herself. There she sat, facing him from a distance, and she wept aloud.
en.R: Then she went and sat down a long way off, about as far as someone can shoot an arrow. She thought, "I will not look while the boy is dying." And she sat there crying loudly.

es.L: Y se fue y se sentó aparte, enfrente, a cierta distancia, como a un tiro de arco, porque dijo: «Que no vea yo la muerte del niño». Y se sentó enfrente, y alzó su voz y lloró.
es.B: Se apartó y se sentó frente a él, a la distancia de un tiro de flecha. «No quiero ver morir al muchacho», se dijo. Allí se quedó sentada, mirándolo desde lejos, y lloró a gritos.
es.R: Luego se fue y se sentó lejos, más o menos a la distancia a la que llega una flecha. Pensaba: «No quiero ver morir a mi hijo». Y se quedó allí sentada, llorando a gritos.

fr.L: Et elle alla s’asseoir à l’écart, en face [de lui], à bonne distance, à environ une portée d’arc, car elle disait : « Que je ne voie pas la mort de l’enfant ! » Et elle s’assit en face [de lui], et elle éleva la voix et pleura.
fr.B: Elle s’éloigna et s’assit en face de lui, à la distance où porte une flèche. « Je ne veux pas voir mourir le garçon », se disait-elle. Elle resta là, assise face à lui à distance, et elle pleura tout haut.
fr.R: Puis elle est allée s’asseoir loin de lui, à peu près à la distance où on peut lancer une flèche. Elle pensait : « Je ne veux pas regarder mon fils mourir. » Et elle est restée là, à pleurer très fort.

sw.L: Akaenda, akaketi peke yake mkabala [naye], mbali kiasi, kama mtupo wa mshale, kwa maana alisema, "Nisione kifo cha mtoto." Akaketi mkabala [naye], akapaza sauti yake, akalia.
sw.B: Akasogea mbali, akaketi akimtazama, umbali wa mtupo wa mshale. Alijiambia, "Sitaki kumtazama kijana akifa." Akakaa pale, akimwelekea kwa mbali, akalia kwa sauti kubwa.
sw.R: Kisha akaenda kuketi mbali sana, karibu umbali ambao mshale unaweza kufika. Alifikiri, "Sitaki kumwona mwanangu akifa." Akakaa pale akilia kwa sauti kubwa.

decisions.choice: about a bowshot away: near enough to see, far enough not to watch
decisions.reason: The distance an arrow carries, perhaps a hundred yards or more. The bow anticipates what Ishmael will become (verse 20).

decisions.choice: she said: she said to herself
decisions.reason: As often, 'said' means thought (20:11).

decisions.choice: she lifted up her voice and wept: the Septuagint has 'the child'
alternatives: and the child lifted up his voice and wept
decisions.reason: The Greek Septuagint reads 'and the child cried aloud and wept', which fits verse 17, 'God heard the voice of the boy'. The Hebrew text, followed here, has Hagar weep.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַנַּעַר֒ וַיִּקְרָא֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀אֶל־הָגָר֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ מַה־לָּ֣ךְ הָגָ֑ר אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֧ע אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל־ק֥וֹל הַנַּ֖עַר בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּא־שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard God the voice of the lad, and called [the] angel of God to Hagar from the heavens and said to her, what [is] to you, Hagar? Do not fear, for has heard God [the] voice of the lad where he [is] there.

en.L: And God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
en.B: God heard the boy's voice, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. "What is wrong, Hagar?" he said. "Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy's voice there where he lies.
en.R: God heard the boy crying. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven. He said, "Hagar, what is the matter? Do not be afraid. God has heard the boy's cries from the place where he is.

es.L: Y oyó Dios la voz del muchacho, y el ángel de Dios llamó a Agar desde el cielo y le dijo: «¿Qué te pasa, Agar? No temas, porque Dios ha oído la voz del muchacho allí donde está.
es.B: Dios oyó la voz del muchacho, y el ángel de Dios llamó a Agar desde el cielo. «¿Qué te ocurre, Agar?», le dijo. «No tengas miedo. Dios ha oído la voz del muchacho allí donde está tendido.
es.R: Dios oyó llorar al muchacho. El ángel de Dios llamó a Agar desde el cielo y le dijo: «Agar, ¿qué te pasa? No tengas miedo. Dios ha oído los gritos del muchacho desde el lugar donde está.

fr.L: Et Dieu entendit la voix du garçon, et l’ange de Dieu appela Agar du haut du ciel et lui dit : « Qu’as-tu, Agar ? Ne crains pas, car Dieu a entendu la voix du garçon là où il est.
fr.B: Dieu entendit la voix du garçon, et l’ange de Dieu appela Agar du ciel. « Qu’y a-t-il, Agar ? lui dit-il. N’aie pas peur. Dieu a entendu la voix du garçon, là où il est couché.
fr.R: Dieu a entendu le garçon pleurer. L’ange de Dieu a appelé Agar depuis le ciel. Il lui a dit : « Agar, qu’est-ce qui ne va pas ? N’aie pas peur. Dieu a entendu les cris du garçon, là où il se trouve.

sw.L: Naye Mungu akasikia sauti ya kijana, na malaika wa Mungu akamwita Hajiri kutoka mbinguni, akamwambia, "Una nini, Hajiri? Usiogope, kwa maana Mungu ameisikia sauti ya kijana pale alipo.
sw.B: Mungu aliisikia sauti ya kijana, na malaika wa Mungu akamwita Hajiri kutoka mbinguni. Akasema, "Una shida gani, Hajiri? Usiogope. Mungu ameisikia sauti ya kijana pale alipolala.
sw.R: Mungu alimsikia kijana akilia. Malaika wa Mungu akamwita Hajiri kutoka mbinguni, akamwambia, "Hajiri, una nini? Usiogope. Mungu amesikia kilio cha kijana kutoka pale alipo.

decisions.choice: God heard: the meaning of Ishmael's name
decisions.reason: Ishmael means 'God hears' (16:11). Hagar wept, yet the text says that God heard the boy. Before he was born, God had heard his mother (16:11); now he hears the son.

decisions.choice: the angel of God called from heaven
decisions.reason: In chapter 16 the angel met Hagar on the road; here he calls from heaven, as he will call to Abraham in 22:11. The angel speaks for God and as God (verse 18, 'I will make him').

decisions.choice: where he is: as he is, where he lies
decisions.reason: God heard the boy in his present helpless state, where Hagar had left him.

decisions.choice: crying ... cries
decisions.reason: Readable says what the boy's 'voice' was: crying out in distress.

source.text: ק֚וּמִי שְׂאִ֣י אֶת־הַנַּ֔עַר וְהַחֲזִ֥יקִי אֶת־יָדֵ֖ךְ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל אֲשִׂימֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Arise, lift up the lad and hold your hand on him, for into a great nation I will make him.

en.L: Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him fast with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation."
en.B: Get up, raise the boy to his feet and take him firmly by the hand. I will make a great nation of him."
en.R: Get up! Go and lift the boy up, and hold his hand. I will make him the father of a great nation."

es.L: Levántate, alza al muchacho y sujétalo con tu mano, porque lo haré una gran nación».
es.B: Levántate, ayuda al muchacho a ponerse en pie y tómalo firmemente de la mano. Yo haré de él una gran nación».
es.R: ¡Levántate! Ve a levantar al muchacho y tómalo de la mano. Yo haré que de él salga una gran nación».

fr.L: Lève-toi, relève le garçon et tiens-le ferme de ta main, car je ferai de lui une grande nation. »
fr.B: Lève-toi, remets le garçon debout et prends-le fermement par la main. Je ferai de lui une grande nation. »
fr.R: Lève-toi ! Va relever le garçon et tiens-lui la main. Je ferai de lui l’ancêtre d’une grande nation. »

sw.L: Inuka, umwinue kijana, umshike kwa mkono wako, kwa maana nitamfanya kuwa taifa kubwa."
sw.B: Inuka, umsimamishe kijana, umshike mkono kwa nguvu. Nitamfanya kuwa taifa kubwa."
sw.R: Inuka! Nenda ukamwinue kijana, umshike mkono. Nitamfanya kuwa baba wa taifa kubwa."

decisions.choice: I will make him a great nation: the angel speaks as God
decisions.reason: The angel speaks in God's own voice. The promise is to 'make him' a great nation, as with Abraham himself (12:2).

decisions.choice: hold him fast with your hand: support and take charge of him
decisions.reason: The phrase means to grip firmly; Hagar is to hold on to the boy and take him forward.

decisions.choice: the father of
decisions.reason: A man becomes a nation through his descendants; Readable says so.

source.text: וַיִּפְקַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־עֵינֶ֔יהָ וַתֵּ֖רֶא בְּאֵ֣ר מָ֑יִם וַתֵּ֜לֶךְ וַתְּמַלֵּ֤א אֶת־הַחֵ֨מֶת֙ מַ֔יִם וַתַּ֖שְׁקְ אֶת־הַנָּֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And opened God her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went and filled the skin [with] water and gave the lad a drink.

en.L: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
en.B: God opened her eyes, and there she saw a well. She went over, filled the skin and gave the boy water to drink.
en.R: Then God helped Hagar see a well nearby. She went and filled the bag with water and gave some to the boy.

es.L: Entonces abrió Dios sus ojos, y ella vio un pozo de agua. Y fue y llenó el odre de agua y dio de beber al muchacho.
es.B: Dios le abrió los ojos, y ella vio allí un pozo. Fue hasta él, llenó el odre y le dio de beber al muchacho.
es.R: Entonces Dios hizo que Agar viera un pozo que estaba cerca. Ella fue, llenó la bolsa de agua y le dio de beber al muchacho.

fr.L: Alors Dieu ouvrit ses yeux, et elle vit un puits d’eau. Et elle alla remplir l’outre d’eau et donna à boire au garçon.
fr.B: Dieu lui ouvrit les yeux, et elle aperçut un puits. Elle y alla, remplit l’outre et fit boire le garçon.
fr.R: Alors Dieu a aidé Agar à voir un puits tout près. Elle est allée remplir l’outre d’eau et elle a donné à boire au garçon.

sw.L: Ndipo Mungu akamfumbua macho, naye akaona kisima cha maji. Akaenda, akakijaza kiriba maji, akamnywesha kijana.
sw.B: Mungu alimfumbua macho, akaona kisima hapo. Akaenda, akakijaza kiriba, akampa kijana maji anywe.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akamsaidia Hajiri kuona kisima karibu. Akaenda akajaza mfuko maji, akampa kijana anywe.

decisions.choice: God opened her eyes: let her see what she had not seen
decisions.reason: The well may have been there all along; God makes her see it (2 Kings 6:17). In 16:13 Hagar named God 'the God who sees'; here he makes her see.

source.text: וַיְהִ֧י אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הַנַּ֖עַר וַיִּגְדָּ֑ל וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיְהִ֖י רֹבֶ֥ה קַשָּֽׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: And was God with the lad, and he grew up and dwelt in the wilderness and became a shooter, an archer.

en.L: And God was with the boy, and he grew up; and he lived in the wilderness and became an archer, a bowman.
en.B: God stayed with the boy while he grew. He settled in the wilderness and became an expert with the bow.
en.R: God took care of the boy as he grew. He made his home in the desert and became very good with a bow and arrows.

es.L: Y Dios estuvo con el muchacho, y él creció; y habitó en el desierto y llegó a ser tirador, arquero.
es.B: Dios acompañó al muchacho mientras crecía. Se estableció en el desierto y llegó a ser un experto con el arco.
es.R: Dios cuidó del muchacho mientras crecía. Vivió en el desierto y llegó a ser muy bueno con el arco y las flechas.

fr.L: Et Dieu fut avec le garçon, et il grandit ; et il habita dans le désert et devint un tireur, un archer.
fr.B: Dieu resta avec le garçon pendant qu’il grandissait. Il s’établit dans le désert et devint un tireur à l’arc habile.
fr.R: Dieu a pris soin du garçon pendant qu’il grandissait. Il a vécu dans le désert et il est devenu très fort au tir à l’arc.

sw.L: Naye Mungu alikuwa pamoja na kijana, akakua; akakaa nyikani, akawa mpiga mishale, mtupa upinde.
sw.B: Mungu alikaa pamoja na kijana alipokuwa akikua. Akaishi nyikani, akawa hodari wa kupiga mishale.
sw.R: Mungu alimtunza kijana alipokuwa akikua. Akaishi jangwani, akawa stadi sana wa kutumia upinde na mishale.

decisions.choice: God was with the boy: God's care continues
decisions.reason: 'God was with' someone means he protected and prospered them, as later with Isaac and Joseph (26:3; 39:2). The son sent away is not outside God's care.

decisions.choice: an archer, a bowman: a skilled hunter
decisions.reason: The exact sense of the first word (roveh) is uncertain, but the phrase means a skilled bowman. Esau, another son who does not carry the promise, is also a hunter (25:27).

source.text: וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּמִדְבַּ֣ר פָּארָ֑ן וַתִּֽקַּֽח־ל֥וֹ אִמּ֛וֹ אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he dwelt in [the] wilderness of Paran, and took for him his mother a wife from [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And he lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
en.B: He made his home in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother found him a wife from Egypt.
en.R: He lived in the Desert of Paran. His mother chose a wife for him from Egypt, her homeland.

es.L: Y habitó en el desierto de Parán, y su madre tomó para él una mujer de la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: Se estableció en el desierto de Parán, y su madre le buscó una esposa de Egipto.
es.R: Vivió en el desierto de Parán. Su madre le escogió una esposa de Egipto, su propio país.

fr.L: Et il habita dans le désert de Parân, et sa mère prit pour lui une femme du pays d’Égypte.
fr.B: Il s’établit dans le désert de Parân, et sa mère lui trouva une femme d’Égypte.
fr.R: Il a vécu dans le désert de Parân. Sa mère lui a choisi une femme en Égypte, son pays d’origine.

sw.L: Naye akakaa katika nyika ya Parani, na mama yake akamtwalia mke kutoka nchi ya Misri.
sw.B: Akaishi katika nyika ya Parani, na mama yake akamtafutia mke kutoka Misri.
sw.R: Aliishi katika jangwa la Parani. Mama yake akamchagulia mke kutoka Misri, nchi yake ya asili.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Paran: the desert south of Canaan
decisions.reason: Paran is the desert region in the north of the Sinai Peninsula, where Israel later wandered (Numbers 10:12; 12:16).

decisions.choice: his mother took a wife for him: an arranged marriage
decisions.reason: Parents arranged marriages. Hagar, an Egyptian (16:1), finds a wife for her son from her own people, as Abraham will find one for Isaac from his own family (24:3-4).

decisions.choice: her homeland
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader that Hagar came from Egypt (16:1).

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־צְבָא֔וֹ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר אֱלֹהִ֣ים עִמְּךָ֔ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֖ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at that time, and said Abimelech and Phicol, [the] commander of his army, to Abraham, saying, God [is] with you in all that you are doing.

en.L: And at that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, "God is with you in all that you do.
en.B: Around that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham: "God is with you in whatever you do.
en.R: At that time Abimelech came to Abraham with Phicol, the commander of his army. Abimelech said, "We can see that God is with you in everything you do.

es.L: Y sucedió en aquel tiempo que dijeron Abimelec y Ficol, el jefe de su ejército, a Abraham: «Dios está contigo en todo lo que haces.
es.B: Por aquel tiempo, Abimelec y Ficol, el jefe de su ejército, le hablaron a Abraham: «Dios está contigo en todo lo que emprendes.
es.R: En ese tiempo, Abimelec fue a ver a Abraham con Ficol, el jefe de su ejército. Abimelec le dijo: «Vemos que Dios está contigo en todo lo que haces.

fr.L: Et il arriva en ce temps-là qu’Abimélek et Picol, le chef de son armée, dirent à Abraham : « Dieu est avec toi dans tout ce que tu fais.
fr.B: Vers ce temps-là, Abimélek et Picol, le chef de son armée, parlèrent à Abraham : « Dieu est avec toi dans tout ce que tu entreprends.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, Abimélek est venu voir Abraham avec Picol, le chef de son armée. Abimélek a dit : « Nous voyons bien que Dieu est avec toi dans tout ce que tu fais.

sw.L: Ikawa wakati ule Abimeleki na Fikoli, jemadari wa jeshi lake, wakamwambia Abrahamu, "Mungu yu pamoja nawe katika yote unayoyafanya.
sw.B: Wakati huo Abimeleki na Fikoli, mkuu wa jeshi lake, walizungumza na Abrahamu: "Mungu yuko pamoja nawe katika kila jambo unalolifanya.
sw.R: Wakati huo Abimeleki alikuja kwa Abrahamu pamoja na Fikoli, mkuu wa jeshi lake. Abimeleki akasema, "Tunaona kwamba Mungu yuko pamoja nawe katika kila kitu unachofanya.

decisions.choice: God is with you: outsiders see the blessing
decisions.reason: The words that have just been said of Ishmael (verse 20) are said of Abraham by a foreign king, who has seen God's protection of him (chapter 20). He comes as one seeking a treaty with a stronger party. In 26:28 Abimelech says the same of Isaac.

decisions.choice: Phicol: a name of unknown meaning
decisions.reason: The name may not be Semitic. The commander of the army comes because a treaty between powers is a matter of security.

decisions.choice: We can see that
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Abimelech speaks from what he has observed.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֨בְעָה לִּ֤י בֵֽאלֹהִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה אִם־תִּשְׁקֹ֣ר לִ֔י וּלְנִינִ֖י וּלְנֶכְדִּ֑י כַּחֶ֜סֶד אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֤יתִי עִמְּךָ֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עִמָּדִ֔י וְעִם־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־גַּ֥רְתָּה בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now swear to me by God here that you will not deal falsely with me and with my offspring and with my posterity; according to the kindness that I have done with you, you will do with me and with the land in which you have sojourned.

en.L: And now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my children or with my descendants, but as I have shown kindness to you, you will show [it] to me and to the land in which you have sojourned."
en.B: So swear to me by God, here and now, that you will never play me false, nor my children, nor their descendants after them. I have kept faith with you; keep faith in the same way with me and with this land where you have made your home as a foreigner."
en.R: So promise me here, with God as your witness, that you will not trick me or my children or my grandchildren. I have been kind to you. Be kind to me in the same way, and to this country where you have been living as an outsider."

es.L: Ahora, pues, júrame aquí por Dios que no me engañarás ni a mí ni a mis hijos ni a mis descendientes, sino que conforme a la bondad que yo he tenido contigo, [la] tendrás tú conmigo y con la tierra en la que has residido como extranjero».
es.B: Así que júrame por Dios, aquí y ahora, que nunca me traicionarás, ni a mí ni a mis hijos ni a los descendientes que vengan después. Yo he sido leal contigo; sé tú leal de la misma manera conmigo y con esta tierra donde vives como extranjero».
es.R: Así que prométeme aquí, con Dios como testigo, que no nos vas a engañar ni a mí ni a mis hijos ni a mis nietos. Yo he sido bueno contigo. Sé tú bueno de la misma manera conmigo y con este país en el que has estado viviendo como forastero».

fr.L: Et maintenant, jure-moi ici par Dieu que tu ne me tromperas ni moi, ni mes enfants, ni ma descendance, mais que selon la bonté que j’ai eue envers toi, tu [en] useras envers moi et envers le pays où tu as séjourné. »
fr.B: Alors jure-moi par Dieu, ici même, que tu ne me trahiras jamais, ni moi, ni mes enfants, ni leurs descendants après eux. Je t’ai été fidèle ; sois fidèle de la même façon envers moi et envers ce pays où tu as vécu en étranger. »
fr.R: Alors promets-moi ici, avec Dieu comme témoin, que tu ne me tromperas pas, ni moi, ni mes enfants, ni mes petits-enfants. J’ai été bon avec toi. Sois bon avec moi de la même façon, et avec ce pays où tu habites comme un étranger. »

sw.L: Basi sasa uniapie hapa kwa Mungu kwamba hutanidanganya mimi, wala watoto wangu, wala wazao wangu; bali kwa kadiri ya wema niliokutendea, utanitendea [vivyo hivyo] mimi na nchi hii uliyokaa ndani yake kama mgeni."
sw.B: Kwa hiyo uniapie kwa Mungu, hapa na sasa, kwamba hutanisaliti kamwe, wala watoto wangu, wala wazao wao baada yao. Mimi nimekuwa mwaminifu kwako; nawe uwe mwaminifu vivyo hivyo kwangu na kwa nchi hii ambamo umeishi kama mgeni."
sw.R: Basi niahidi hapa, Mungu akiwa shahidi, kwamba hutanidanganya mimi wala watoto wangu wala wajukuu wangu. Nimekutendea wema. Nawe unitendee wema vivyo hivyo, mimi na nchi hii ambamo umekuwa ukiishi kama mgeni."

decisions.choice: swear by God: an oath with God as witness
decisions.reason: An oath called on God to witness the promise and to punish the one who broke it. The name of the place, Beersheba, will come from this oath (verse 31).

decisions.choice: my children and my descendants (nin, neked): all who come after me
decisions.reason: The two words are a fixed pair for a man's line of descendants (Job 18:19; Isaiah 14:22). Abimelech wants a treaty that will last for generations.

decisions.choice: kindness (chesed): loyalty under an agreement
decisions.reason: The same word as in 20:13: the faithful conduct owed within a relationship. Abimelech had treated Abraham generously (20:14-15) and asks for the same in return.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אָנֹכִ֖י אִשָּׁבֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abraham, I will swear.

en.L: And Abraham said, "I will swear."
en.B: Abraham replied, "I give you my oath."
en.R: Abraham said, "I will swear to it."

es.L: Y dijo Abraham: «Yo juraré».
es.B: Abraham respondió: «Te doy mi juramento».
es.R: Abraham dijo: «Te lo juro».

fr.L: Et Abraham dit : « Moi, je jurerai. »
fr.B: Abraham répondit : « Je te le jure. »
fr.R: Abraham a dit : « Je vais te le promettre par serment. »

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akasema, "Mimi nitaapa."
sw.B: Abrahamu akajibu, "Nakuapia."
sw.R: Abrahamu akasema, "Ndiyo, nitakuapia."

source.text: וְהוֹכִ֥חַ אַבְרָהָ֖ם אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ עַל־אֹדוֹת֙ בְּאֵ֣ר הַמַּ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּזְל֖וּ עַבְדֵ֥י אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And reproved Abraham Abimelech on account of the well of water which had seized [the] servants of Abimelech.

en.L: And Abraham reproved Abimelech about the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.
en.B: Abraham, however, took Abimelech to task over a well that Abimelech's men had taken from him by force.
en.R: But Abraham had a complaint against Abimelech. Abimelech's men had taken over one of Abraham's wells.

es.L: Y Abraham reprendió a Abimelec a causa del pozo de agua que los siervos de Abimelec habían tomado por la fuerza.
es.B: Abraham, sin embargo, le reclamó a Abimelec por un pozo que los hombres de Abimelec le habían quitado por la fuerza.
es.R: Pero Abraham tenía una queja contra Abimelec. Los hombres de Abimelec se habían apoderado de uno de los pozos de Abraham.

fr.L: Et Abraham fit des reproches à Abimélek au sujet du puits d’eau dont les serviteurs d’Abimélek s’étaient emparés.
fr.B: Abraham, cependant, demanda des comptes à Abimélek au sujet d’un puits que les hommes d’Abimélek lui avaient pris de force.
fr.R: Mais Abraham avait une plainte contre Abimélek. Les hommes d’Abimélek avaient pris un des puits d’Abraham.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akamlaumu Abimeleki kwa ajili ya kisima cha maji ambacho watumwa wa Abimeleki walikuwa wamekinyang'anya.
sw.B: Hata hivyo Abrahamu alimlalamikia Abimeleki kuhusu kisima ambacho watu wa Abimeleki walikuwa wamemnyang'anya kwa nguvu.
sw.R: Lakini Abrahamu alikuwa na malalamiko dhidi ya Abimeleki. Watu wa Abimeleki walikuwa wamechukua kimoja cha visima vya Abrahamu.

decisions.choice: reproved (hokhiach): raised a complaint
decisions.reason: The verb means to argue a case or call someone to account. Before the oath is sworn, Abraham brings up a wrong that must be put right.

decisions.choice: the well: water rights in a dry land
decisions.reason: In the Negev a well meant life for flocks and herds, and wells were fought over (26:15-22). Whoever dug a well claimed the right to it.

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: The word (eved) may mean slaves or a king's officers; Balanced and Readable say 'men', since the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: one of Abraham's wells
decisions.reason: Readable says whose well it was; verse 30 shows Abraham had dug it.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִ֥י עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְגַם־אַתָּ֞ה לֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֗י וְגַ֧ם אָנֹכִ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בִּלְתִּ֥י הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abimelech, I do not know who has done this thing; and also you did not tell me, and also I did not hear except today.

en.L: And Abimelech said, "I do not know who has done this thing. You did not tell me, and I did not hear of it until today."
en.B: Abimelech said, "I have no idea who did this. You never told me, and this is the first I have heard of it."
en.R: Abimelech said, "I do not know who did this. You never told me about it. This is the first time I have heard of it."

es.L: Y dijo Abimelec: «No sé quién ha hecho esto; tampoco tú me lo dijiste, ni yo lo había oído hasta hoy».
es.B: Abimelec respondió: «No tengo idea de quién hizo esto. Tú nunca me lo dijiste, y es la primera vez que oigo hablar de ello».
es.R: Abimelec dijo: «No sé quién hizo esto. Tú nunca me lo contaste. Es la primera vez que lo oigo».

fr.L: Et Abimélek dit : « Je ne sais pas qui a fait cette chose ; toi non plus, tu ne me l’as pas dit, et moi non plus, je n’en ai pas entendu parler, sauf aujourd’hui. »
fr.B: Abimélek répondit : « Je n’ai aucune idée de qui a fait cela. Tu ne me l’as jamais dit, et c’est la première fois que j’en entends parler. »
fr.R: Abimélek a dit : « Je ne sais pas qui a fait cela. Tu ne m’en as jamais parlé. C’est la première fois que j’en entends parler. »

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akasema, "Sijui ni nani aliyefanya jambo hili; wala wewe hukuniambia, wala mimi sikusikia ila leo."
sw.B: Abimeleki akasema, "Sijui kabisa ni nani aliyefanya hivi. Hukuniambia kamwe, na hii ndiyo mara ya kwanza ninasikia habari hii."
sw.R: Abimeleki akasema, "Sijui ni nani aliyefanya hivyo. Hukuwahi kuniambia. Hii ni mara ya kwanza ninasikia jambo hili."

decisions.choice: you did not tell me, and I did not hear: a threefold denial
decisions.reason: Three times Abimelech says 'not': he did not know, Abraham did not tell, he did not hear. He clears himself of the wrong and implies that Abraham should have spoken sooner.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Abraham sheep and cattle and gave [them] to Abimelech, and made the two of them a covenant.

en.L: And Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave [them] to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
en.B: Abraham then presented Abimelech with sheep and cattle, and the two of them entered into a covenant.
en.R: Then Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, and the two of them made a covenant with each other.

es.L: Y tomó Abraham ovejas y vacas y [se las] dio a Abimelec, e hicieron los dos un pacto.
es.B: Entonces Abraham le regaló a Abimelec ovejas y ganado, y los dos sellaron un pacto.
es.R: Luego Abraham le dio a Abimelec algunas ovejas y vacas, y los dos hicieron un pacto entre sí.

fr.L: Et Abraham prit des moutons et des bœufs et [les] donna à Abimélek, et ils conclurent tous les deux une alliance.
fr.B: Abraham offrit alors à Abimélek du petit et du gros bétail, et tous deux conclurent une alliance.
fr.R: Ensuite, Abraham a donné à Abimélek des moutons et des bœufs, et ils ont fait une alliance tous les deux.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akatwaa kondoo na ng'ombe, akampa Abimeleki, nao wawili wakafanya agano.
sw.B: Kisha Abrahamu akampa Abimeleki kondoo na ng'ombe, nao wawili wakaingia katika agano.
sw.R: Halafu Abrahamu akampa Abimeleki kondoo na ng'ombe kadhaa, na wale wawili wakafanya agano wao kwa wao.

decisions.choice: made a covenant: literally 'cut a covenant'
decisions.reason: The verb (karat) means 'cut', perhaps from the animals cut in two when a covenant was made (15:9-18). A covenant here is a sworn treaty between two parties.

decisions.choice: Abraham gave sheep and cattle: gifts that seal the treaty
decisions.reason: As Abimelech had given gifts to Abraham (20:14), Abraham now gives to him; the gifts confirm the agreement.

source.text: וַיַּצֵּ֣ב אַבְרָהָ֗ם אֶת־שֶׁ֛בַע כִּבְשֹׂ֥ת הַצֹּ֖אן לְבַדְּהֶֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And set Abraham seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.

en.L: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock apart by themselves.
en.B: Then Abraham took seven young ewes from the flock and placed them to one side.
en.R: Abraham also took seven female lambs from his flock and put them off by themselves.

es.L: Y puso Abraham siete corderas del rebaño aparte.
es.B: Después Abraham tomó siete corderas del rebaño y las puso a un lado.
es.R: Abraham también tomó siete ovejas jóvenes de su rebaño y las apartó de las demás.

fr.L: Et Abraham mit à part sept agnelles du troupeau.
fr.B: Puis Abraham prit sept jeunes brebis du troupeau et les plaça à l’écart.
fr.R: Abraham a aussi pris sept petites brebis de son troupeau et il les a mises à part.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akaweka kando wana-kondoo wa kike saba wa kundi peke yao.
sw.B: Kisha Abrahamu akachukua kondoo wachanga wa kike saba kutoka kundini, akawaweka kando.
sw.R: Abrahamu pia akachukua kondoo wadogo wa kike saba kutoka kundi lake, akawaweka peke yao.

decisions.choice: seven (sheva): a play on 'oath'
decisions.reason: The Hebrew for 'seven' (sheva) sounds like the verb 'swear' (nishba). The seven lambs and the oath together give the place its name (verse 31).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֑ם מָ֣ה הֵ֗נָּה שֶׁ֤בַע כְּבָשֹׂת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִצַּ֖בְתָּ לְבַדָּֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abimelech to Abraham, what [are] these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?

en.L: And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What are these seven ewe lambs here that you have set by themselves?"
en.B: Abimelech asked Abraham, "Why have you put these seven lambs off to one side?"
en.R: Abimelech asked, "What are these seven lambs for? Why did you put them by themselves?"

es.L: Y dijo Abimelec a Abraham: «¿Qué [significan] estas siete corderas que has puesto aparte?».
es.B: Abimelec le preguntó a Abraham: «¿Por qué has puesto aparte estas siete corderas?».
es.R: Abimelec preguntó: «¿Para qué son estas siete ovejas? ¿Por qué las pusiste aparte?».

fr.L: Et Abimélek dit à Abraham : « Que [sont] ces sept agnelles que tu as mises à part ? »
fr.B: Abimélek demanda à Abraham : « Pourquoi as-tu mis ces sept agnelles à l’écart ? »
fr.R: Abimélek a demandé : « À quoi servent ces sept brebis ? Pourquoi les as-tu mises à part ? »

sw.L: Naye Abimeleki akamwambia Abrahamu, "Hawa wana-kondoo wa kike saba uliowaweka peke yao [ni wa] nini?"
sw.B: Abimeleki akamwuliza Abrahamu, "Kwa nini umewaweka kando kondoo hawa saba?"
sw.R: Abimeleki akauliza, "Kondoo hawa saba ni wa nini? Kwa nini umewaweka peke yao?"

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֚י אֶת־שֶׁ֣בַע כְּבָשֹׂ֔ת תִּקַּ֖ח מִיָּדִ֑י בַּעֲבוּר֙ תִּֽהְיֶה־לִּ֣י לְעֵדָ֔ה כִּ֥י חָפַ֖רְתִּי אֶת־הַבְּאֵ֥ר הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, for the seven ewe lambs you will take from my hand, so that it will be for me a witness that I dug this well.

en.L: And he said, "These seven ewe lambs you shall take from my hand, so that it may be a witness for me that I dug this well."
en.B: He answered, "Take these seven lambs from me. They will stand as my proof that I am the one who dug this well."
en.R: Abraham answered, "Take these seven lambs from me. Then everyone will know that I dug this well and that it belongs to me."

es.L: Y dijo: «Estas siete corderas tomarás de mi mano, para que me sirvan de testimonio de que yo cavé este pozo».
es.B: Él respondió: «Acepta de mí estas siete corderas. Servirán de prueba de que fui yo quien cavó este pozo».
es.R: Abraham le respondió: «Recibe de mí estas siete ovejas. Así todos sabrán que yo cavé este pozo y que es mío».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Ces sept agnelles, tu les prendras de ma main, afin que cela me serve de témoignage que j’ai creusé ce puits. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « Accepte de ma main ces sept agnelles. Elles prouveront que c’est moi qui ai creusé ce puits. »
fr.R: Abraham a répondu : « Prends ces sept brebis de ma part. Comme ça, tout le monde saura que j’ai creusé ce puits et qu’il est à moi. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Wana-kondoo hawa wa kike saba utawapokea kutoka mkononi mwangu, ili kwangu kiwe ushahidi kwamba mimi nilichimba kisima hiki."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Wapokee kondoo hawa saba kutoka kwangu. Watakuwa ushahidi wangu kwamba mimi ndiye niliyechimba kisima hiki."
sw.R: Abrahamu akajibu, "Pokea kondoo hawa saba kutoka kwangu. Hapo kila mtu atajua kwamba nilichimba kisima hiki, na kwamba ni changu."

decisions.choice: you shall take from my hand ... a witness: accepting the gift accepts the claim
decisions.reason: By accepting the lambs in front of witnesses, Abimelech would publicly recognize that the well belonged to Abraham. Ownership was confirmed by a public act, not by a written deed.

decisions.choice: and that it belongs to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the proof was for: Abraham's right to the well.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֗ן קָרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע כִּ֛י שָׁ֥ם נִשְׁבְּע֖וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore he called the place that Beersheba, for there swore the two of them.

en.L: Therefore he called that place Beersheba, for there the two of them swore.
en.B: That is why the place was named Beersheba: the two of them took an oath there.
en.R: So that place was called Beersheba, which means "well of the oath" or "well of seven." It got that name because the two men made a solemn promise to each other there.

es.L: Por eso llamó a aquel lugar Beerseba, porque allí juraron los dos.
es.B: Por eso aquel lugar recibió el nombre de Beerseba: allí los dos hicieron un juramento.
es.R: Por eso aquel lugar se llamó Beerseba, que quiere decir «pozo del juramento» o «pozo de los siete». Recibió ese nombre porque allí los dos hombres se hicieron una promesa solemne.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi il appela ce lieu Beer-Shéba, car là ils jurèrent tous les deux.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi ce lieu reçut le nom de Beer-Shéba : c’est là que tous deux prêtèrent serment.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que cet endroit s’est appelé Beer-Shéba, ce qui veut dire « puits du serment » ou « puits des sept ». Il a reçu ce nom parce que les deux hommes s’y étaient fait une promesse solennelle.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo akapaita mahali pale Beer-sheba, kwa sababu pale wale wawili waliapa.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu mahali pale paliitwa Beer-sheba: wale wawili waliapa kiapo pale.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mahali pale paliitwa Beer-sheba, maana yake "kisima cha kiapo" au "kisima cha saba." Palipata jina hilo kwa sababu wale watu wawili waliahidiana pale kwa kiapo.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: 'well of the oath' or 'well of seven'
decisions.reason: Beer means well, and sheba can mean both 'seven' and 'oath'. The name recalls the seven lambs (verses 28-30) and the oath (verse 31). Isaac later renews the name (26:33).

decisions.choice: which means "well of the oath" or "well of seven"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name so the reason given makes sense (m1).

source.text: וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיָּ֣קָם אֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וּפִיכֹל֙ שַׂר־צְבָא֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they made a covenant at Beersheba; and arose Abimelech and Phicol, [the] commander of his army, and returned to [the] land of [the] Philistines.

en.L: So they made a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army rose and returned to the land of the Philistines.
en.B: Once the covenant at Beersheba was made, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol got up and went home to the land of the Philistines.
en.R: When the covenant was made at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol left. They returned to the land of the Philistines.

es.L: Así hicieron un pacto en Beerseba. Y se levantaron Abimelec y Ficol, el jefe de su ejército, y volvieron a la tierra de los filisteos.
es.B: Una vez hecho el pacto en Beerseba, Abimelec y Ficol, el jefe de su ejército, se pusieron en camino y regresaron a la tierra de los filisteos.
es.R: Cuando hicieron el pacto en Beerseba, Abimelec y Ficol se fueron. Regresaron a la tierra de los filisteos.

fr.L: Ainsi ils conclurent une alliance à Beer-Shéba. Puis Abimélek et Picol, le chef de son armée, se levèrent et retournèrent au pays des Philistins.
fr.B: Une fois l’alliance conclue à Beer-Shéba, Abimélek et Picol, le chef de son armée, se mirent en route et rentrèrent au pays des Philistins.
fr.R: Quand l’alliance a été faite à Beer-Shéba, Abimélek et Picol sont partis. Ils sont retournés au pays des Philistins.

sw.L: Basi wakafanya agano huko Beer-sheba. Kisha Abimeleki na Fikoli, jemadari wa jeshi lake, wakaondoka, wakarudi katika nchi ya Wafilisti.
sw.B: Baada ya agano kufanywa huko Beer-sheba, Abimeleki na Fikoli, mkuu wa jeshi lake, waliondoka, wakarudi nyumbani katika nchi ya Wafilisti.
sw.R: Walipokwisha kufanya agano huko Beer-sheba, Abimeleki na Fikoli waliondoka. Wakarudi katika nchi ya Wafilisti.

decisions.choice: the land of the Philistines: the coastal region later known by that name
decisions.reason: The Philistines best known in the Bible settled on the southern coast around 1200 BC, long after Abraham's day. The narrator uses the name by which the region and its people were later known; it may also refer to an earlier group of the same name (26:1).

source.text: וַיִּטַּ֥ע אֶ֖שֶׁל בִּבְאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיִּ֨קְרָא־שָׁ֔ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֵ֥ל עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he planted a tamarisk in Beersheba, and called there on [the] name of YHWH, God of eternity.

en.L: And he planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and called there on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Everlasting God.
en.B: Abraham planted a tamarisk at Beersheba. There he worshiped, calling on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God Everlasting.
en.R: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. There he worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who lives forever.

es.L: Y plantó un tamarisco en Beerseba, e invocó allí el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de eternidad.
es.B: Abraham plantó un tamarisco en Beerseba. Allí adoró, invocando el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios eterno.
es.R: Abraham plantó un tamarisco en Beerseba. Allí adoró {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios que vive para siempre.

fr.L: Et il planta un tamaris à Beer-Shéba, et il invoqua là le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’éternité.
fr.B: Abraham planta un tamaris à Beer-Shéba. Là, il adora en invoquant le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu éternel.
fr.R: Abraham a planté un tamaris à Beer-Shéba. Là, il a adoré {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu qui vit pour toujours.

sw.L: Naye akapanda mkwaju huko Beer-sheba, akaliitia hapo jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa milele.
sw.B: Abrahamu alipanda mkwaju huko Beer-sheba. Hapo akaabudu, akiliitia jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Milele.
sw.R: Abrahamu alipanda mti wa mkwaju huko Beer-sheba. Hapo akamwabudu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu anayeishi milele.

decisions.choice: a tamarisk: a hardy desert tree
decisions.reason: The tamarisk grows in dry ground and gives shade for many years. Planting one was a sign that Abraham meant to stay; trees often marked places of worship and meeting (12:6; 1 Samuel 22:6).

decisions.choice: the Everlasting God (El Olam)
decisions.reason: Olam means a time without limit. Abraham names the LORD as the God who lasts forever (Isaiah 40:28), beside a treaty meant to last for generations (verse 23).

decisions.choice: called on the name of the LORD: worshiped
decisions.reason: To call on God's name is to pray to him and worship him (4:26; 12:8; 26:25).

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: The subject is supplied; the Hebrew says 'he'.

decisions.choice: worshiped
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (m3).

decisions.choice: "mkwaju"
decisions.reason: The tamarisk has no everyday Swahili name. "Mkwaju" is the name Swahili Bible readers know for this tree, but it properly names the tamarind, a different tree; a native reviewer should decide whether a descriptive phrase or the loan "tamariski" is better.

source.text: וַיָּ֧גָר אַבְרָהָ֛ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And sojourned Abraham in [the] land of [the] Philistines many days.

en.L: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
en.B: For a long time after that, Abraham lived as a resident foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
en.R: Abraham stayed on in the land of the Philistines for a long time, living there as an outsider.

es.L: Y residió Abraham como extranjero en la tierra de los filisteos muchos días.
es.B: Durante mucho tiempo después, Abraham vivió como extranjero residente en la tierra de los filisteos.
es.R: Abraham se quedó mucho tiempo en la tierra de los filisteos, viviendo allí como forastero.

fr.L: Et Abraham séjourna dans le pays des Philistins de nombreux jours.
fr.B: Longtemps encore, Abraham vécut en résident étranger au pays des Philistins.
fr.R: Abraham est resté longtemps au pays des Philistins, et il y a vécu comme un étranger.

sw.L: Naye Abrahamu akakaa ugenini katika nchi ya Wafilisti siku nyingi.
sw.B: Kwa muda mrefu baadaye, Abrahamu aliishi kama mgeni mkazi katika nchi ya Wafilisti.
sw.R: Abrahamu aliendelea kukaa katika nchi ya Wafilisti kwa muda mrefu, akiishi pale kama mgeni.

decisions.choice: sojourned: lived as a foreigner
decisions.reason: Even with a well and a treaty, Abraham remains a resident foreigner in the land promised to his descendants (20:1; 23:4).
